entries.title: Bears match Seahawks' physicality, lead at halftime
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — In their first game since they declared their postseason dreams to the rest of the league, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> did something to the Seahawks that no one had done in 27 games: they scored on the first drive.</p><p>And what a drive it was: 17 plays for 80 grueling yards over a whopping eight minutes and 32 seconds. Receiver Luther Burden’s fourth catch of the drive was his shortest — a 1-yard touchdown.</p><p>With that, the Bears proved that they could do one of the toughest things in the sport — match the physicality of the defending Super Bowl champions. When the Bears ran into the locker room with a 13-9 lead, it was clear that the Bears were who they believe themselves to be: contenders for the NFC title.</p><p>Quarterback Caleb Williams hung in the pocket and delivered throw after throw with a hand in his face, finishing the half 17-for-25 for 165 yards and a 99.6 passer rating. The Bears had 208 yards in the first half against a Seahawks defense that, thus far this season, had allowed 234 per game.</p><p>Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, for whom the Bears sent the Titans two first round picks and a fourth-rounder last week, made his presence known early, sacking Sam Darnold in the first quarter. His new teammates matched his intensity, allowing only three first downs on the Seahawks’ five possessions before their touchdown-scoring drive. He led the Bears with five tackles in the first half, a rare feat for a defensive tackle.</p><p>The two sides traded second-quarter field goals, a 27-yard Jason Myers kick into the north end zone and a 44-yard Cairo Santos boot into the north end.</p><p>The Bears took over at the Seahawks 28 with about five minutes to play and marched downfield with relative ease. Rome Odunze caught an 18-yard pass, his first of the game. Two plays later, the Bears snapped the ball to running back D’Andre Swift, who handed off to Williams, who was lined up in the left slot, on a reverse. Williams pulled up and threw to Odunze, who was lined up left and ran a post route, for 24 yards.</p><p>Left with fourth-and-two from the Seahawks’ 20 with 1:12 left in the first half, the Bears lined up and let Williams try to draw Seattle offside on a hard count. When the Seahawks wouldn’t jump, Ben Johnson called a timeout and Santos came out to make a 38-yard field goal.</p><p>The Seahawks took possession and scored their first touchdown of the game with 30 seconds left after superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba beat Tyrique Stevenson on a deep ball down the left sideline for a 43-yard touchdown. Smith-Njigba, who entered the weekend as the NFL’s receiving yards leader, had four catches for 92 yards in the first half.</p><p>Myers then missed the extra point.</p>

entries.title: Bears notebook: QB Caleb Williams wears logo-less Caddix cleats vs. Seahawks to avoid more trouble with NFL
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback <b>Caleb Williams</b> relented in his confrontation with the NFL over his cleats by wearing an all-black, logo-less pair Monday against the Seahawks.</p><p>The league <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/25/bears-qb-caleb-williams-fined-11-941-for-wearing-tom-brady-backed-caddix-cleats-another-fine-likely-coming" >fined Williams a total of $35,823 for wearing Caddix cleats</a> with a noticeable logo in recent games against the Falcons and Patriots because it violated its partnership with Nike, Under Armour and adidas. Players are not allowed to promote any non-partner brands on game days.</p><p>Rather than digging in harder, perhaps following former Bears quarterback <b>Jim McMahon</b>’s famous move of writing commissioner <b>Pete Rozelle</b>’s name on his headband after Rozelle fined him for an unauthorized adidas headband, Williams sought to make peace before it turned into an issue in which the league could prevent him from taking the field.</p><p>The NFL’s rulebook has a section that says officials can bar a player from playing if they have a uniform violation, and when asked about it leading up to the Seattle game, Bears coach <b>Ben Johnson</b> said he was confident Williams wouldn’t do anything that would hurt the team.</p><p>Caddix has seized on the marketing momentum of Williams putting their cleats in the spotlight and bought billboard space in Chicago advertising that it is paying his fines. When a video surfaced of Williams wearing his unmarked cleats in pre-game warmups, the company’s X account posted, “No logo necessary!”</p><p>Caddix says roughly 60 players are wearing its cleats this season, and Williams has been adamant about sticking with them because he believes in their claim that they reduce non-contact knee and ankle injuries.</p><p>He wore an all-white version of the cleats in the preseason and in his first two games, including when he hurt his hamstring, and the company’s logo didn’t stand out enough to bother the NFL.</p><p>Williams does not have an endorsement deal with Caddix or any other brand in order to maintain freedom to wear whatever he pleases. He also has worn Nike and New Balance shoes in his career.</p><h3><b>Bagent on block?</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Bears are unlikely to make any more splashy trades after acquiring defensive tackle <b>Jeffery Simmons</b> — <b>Khalil Mack</b> is still a possibility — but there’s a good chance they’ll get called about backup quarterback <b>Tyson Bagent</b>.</p><p>The Ravens lost starter <b>Lamar Jackson</b>, possibly for the season, and backup <b>Tyler Huntley</b> this week and probably don’t want to concede their season at 4-4 in the wide-open AFC North. Plus, former Bears assistant <b>Declan Doyle</b> is their offensive coordinator.</p><h3><b>Simmons tribute</b></h3><h3></h3><p> Simmons started for the Bears in his debut, but his old team hasn’t forgotten him. Several Titans defenders wore red arm sleeves Sunday against the Bengals in their first game without him — a nod to Simmons’ trademark.</p><p>“We just wanted to let Jeff know we’re thinking of him and we love him,” defensive end <b>Solomon Thomas</b> said. “He was an unbelievable leader... I've never seen a player of his caliber work the way he works.</p><p>"When someone like that leaves your room, you can’t just move on from it. We wanted to show him how much he means to us.”</p><h3><b>Muhammad out</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Bears rookie cornerback <b>Malik Muhammad</b>, who has developed into a starter, was out with toe injury. It was his first missed game.</p>

entries.title: Veteran big man Nic Claxton moves closer to making his Bulls debut
entries.summary: <p>PHILADELPHIA – Help is on the way … finally.</p><p>And the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" >Bulls</a> could use it. Then again, who couldn’t use a 6-foot-11 athletic big who protects the basket and is an elite rim runner?</p><p>Coach <b>Tiago Splitter</b> said Monday that offseason acquisition <b>Nic Claxton</b> went through a full practice Sunday — his first since he injured his hamstring just before the start of training camp.</p><p>“He’s working with the team,” Splitter said. “We had a good practice — not long, but short and intense, and he was able to be in the entire practice with the guys, and that’s a good sign. He’s progressing with the plan, and we’ll figure out the best game for him to come back.”</p><p>The Bulls face the Knicks on Wednesday in New York, then have a three-game homestand against the 76ers, Spurs and Hawks. Splitter was leaning toward a return sometime in that span as long as there are no setbacks.</p><p>“It could be, yeah,” he said.</p><p>What will Claxton add? Initially, he’s likely to play on restricted minutes and come off the bench. But if the Bulls get the apex version of Claxton from his days as a starting center for the Nets, they’ll instantly have a much better defense just from a rim-protection standpoint. Claxton averaged 2.5 blocks per game in the 2022-23 season in Brooklyn and 2.1 the next season.</p><p>He’ll also give the Bulls another long athlete in transition, creating another lob-threat option for guards such as <b>Josh Giddey</b> and <b>Tre Jones</b>.</p><p>The only unknown is who would be bumped out of the rotation. Splitter has been using a second unit of <b>Zach Collins</b>, <b>Isaac Okoro</b>, Jones, <b>Noa Essengue</b> and <b>Leonard Miller</b>. If Claxton is used as a starter, <b>Jalen Smith</b> drops down to a second-unit spot, and Splitter already has said he leans on a 10-man rotation at most. That means Miller and Essengue likely would compete to keep the final spot.</p><p><b>Speaking of . . .</b></p><p>As the Bulls continue to help Essengue find a path to keeping a rotation role, his job for now is simple: Play defense and more defense and worry about the other stuff later. He’s being put on opposing perimeter players and picking up some guards full-court.</p><p>“He can slide in front of people, he’s long, [and] he and Isaac are the best on our team at doing that,” Splitter said. “He can pick up guys at full-court. Just his ability to move his feet — it’s elite, to be honest.</p><p>“He still makes mistakes. He’s a 19-year-old kid that is learning to compete at the highest level. [But] I think he can be a tremendous defensive player one day in<br>this league.”</p><p><b>The kids can take it</b></p><p>There’s a reason individual Bulls players haven’t had many days off. Splitter and his coaching staff believe there’s simply too much work to do — too many pieces of his installation they’re still working to learn.</p><p>It helps that this team is made up of mostly young players who don’t need days off in the early part of the season like older players might.</p><p>“I think it’s a young team, [and] they have the legs to do that,” Splitter said. “A vet is different, a vet team. We’ve got to work, we’ve got to get better, and I’d rather have them a little bit sore in a game than not putting in the work.”</p>

entries.title: First day of practice: Marmion goes co-ed, jumps straight into the fire with a varsity girls basketball team
entries.summary: <p>After averaging more than 20 wins across 25 seasons in stops at IC Catholic, Lisle and Marian Catholic, Dan Murray stepped away from coaching girls basketball last year.</p><p>But it was a pause rather than a hard stop. Murray joined the faculty at Marmion and laid the foundation for the first girls team in the school's 93-year history.</p><p>Marmion has gone co-ed, admitting around 40 freshmen and sophomore girls this school year. The 11 who are on the girls basketball team got to work Monday as practice opened around the state.</p><p>"I'll be honest with you," Murray told the Sun-Times during a break in practice. "It was very difficult last year, not coaching and not being in it after so long. And obviously it's something I love to do. It really lets you know how much it means to you."</p><p>Marmion is adding a few other girls sports this school year and will start more next year as more girls enroll. Most will start at the junior-varsity level, but Murray and his players are jumping right into the fire. They'll play a varsity schedule and will be in Class 3A for the IHSA playoffs.</p><p>"We did want kids to know that we were taking this very seriously in terms of wanting to build a strong program," Murray said. "Hopefully kids who really love the game of basketball and aspire to do some things at the high school level and possibly beyond would take a look at us."</p><div class="Enhancement" entries.title: Blackhawks debut new green Hometown Remix jerseys to tepid fan reaction
entries.summary: <p>The Blackhawks debuted their new green jerseys — a not-so-well-kept secret for the last several weeks — on Monday against the Avalanche.</p><p>They’re quite similar to the jerseys the Hawks used to wear for St. Patrick’s Day before the NHL banned specialty warmup jerseys in 2023. The color theme is built out from the green second feather in the primary logo, and the shoulders are adorned with the alternate ‘‘crossed C’’ logo.</p><p>Those green St. Patrick’s jerseys long have been popular, and you typically will see a few fans donning them at the United Center at any given game. In the past, not many NHL teams had been able to pull off a color outside their usual scheme so well.</p><p>But that changed Monday with the official release of the Hometown Remix, Fanatics’ new set of alternate jerseys for all 32 teams.</p><p>There are some striking looks in the collection. The Panthers nailed their pink ‘‘Miami Vice’’ sweater, as did the Ducks with their green, purple and yellow ‘‘Mighty Ducks’’ sweater. The Kings now have a new purple throwback jersey, the Bruins now have a brown jersey and a bunch of teams now have black jerseys with vivid accents.</p><p>The originality and creativity of many of those jerseys likely contributed to a lackluster fan reaction toward the Hawks’ new green sweaters, considering those already have been done before in almost identical form. They’re also quite similar to the Stars’ regular home jerseys, which many people pointed out.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Here are the official photos of the Blackhawks’ new green Hometown Remix jersey, which they’ll debut tonight against the Avalanche.<br><br>Also wearing them 12/29 vs Vegas and four times in March.<br><br>Thoughts? <a href="https://t.co/lM3VjLy2zu">pic.twitter.com/lM3VjLy2zu</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2117271752397205563?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 2, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>It’s worth noting there are a few differences from the old St. Patrick’s jerseys. The secondary color is tan, not white, and the collar is now black (with tan laces below it). Four stars — like those in the Chicago flag — are embossed into the sleeve stripes. I personally liked the brownish-tan gloves the Hawks wore Monday.</p><p>But Hawks fans have been inundated with jersey releases lately, considering the team wore special red centennial jerseys last season and debuted new black jerseys — a nostalgic throwback to the 1990s — last November that remain in the rotation this season.</p><p>And given the Hawks’ on-ice struggles, it simply might be impossible for the fan base to get too excited about anything right now.</p><p>The Hawks will wear these new green jerseys again Dec. 29 against the Golden Knights, plus four times between March 8 and March 16 leading up to St. Patrick’s Day. They typically wear their black alternate jerseys on Fridays.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="113" height="200" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/N6StHPgRXdc?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="Blackhawks debut their new green uniforms"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p><b>Internal data</b></p><p>Hawks coach Jeff Blashill's morning news conference Monday contained a couple interesting tidbits.</p><p>The first pertained to the team's games last week against the Kings and Bruins, which Blashill said were "two of the top five games we've had in the last four years" based on a stat they track internally called "on-puck action...which basically measures execution offensively."</p><p>The Hawks haven't played many great games over the last four years, which sets a low bar. And they did play very well in those two games last week, despite losing to the Bruins. In between, their "on-puck action" in the Red Wings game was surely much worse.</p><p><b>Three centers</b></p><p>The second interesting tidbit pertained to Connor Bedard, Frank Nazar and Anton Frondell all playing center, with Blashill squashing any hopes of Frondell moving up to Bedard's wing anytime soon.</p><p>"[I'm] not in a hurry to move any of those guys out of their natural positions," he said. "Ultimately, you have to have three dangerous lines...or at least three lines with big roles in this league to be a really good team."</p>

entries.title: Quincy man accused of mailing suspicious letters to elected officials to remain in custody
entries.summary: <p>A Quincy man accused of sending suspicious letters to members of Congress will remain in custody while awaiting trial after waiving his right to fight prosecutors' bid to keep him detained.</p><p>Matthew Unglesbee, 36, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/10/26/quincy-man-charged-mailed-letters-white-powder-congress-members-unglesbee" target="_blank" ><u>faces charges</u></a> of mailing threatening communications, false information and hoaxes, according to the complaint filed in the Central District of Illinois. A jury trial is set to begin Dec. 7.</p><p>Unglesbee told a judge he understood the decision and had not been threatened or offered anything in exchange for the decision.</p><p>“We will concede to detention,” federal public defender Roxanne Mendez Johnson said at a hearing Monday. Johnson has been appointed to represent Unglesbee.</p><p>The charges follow several <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/10/16/schneider-quigleys-offices-receive-suspicious-letters-amid-pre-election-threats" target="_blank" ><u>Illinois lawmakers reporting receiving suspicious mail</u></a> in recent weeks, including Democratic U.S. Reps. Mike Quigley, Brad Schneider and Jan Schakowsky.</p><p>Sen. Tammy Duckworth’s Chicago office also confirmed receiving two suspicious letters in recent weeks.</p><p>During an interview with law enforcement, Unglesbee allegedly admitted in writing that he sent letters containing a white, granular substance and handwritten messages, including “HA HA” and “HAH enjoy the gift,” according to an FBI affidavit. While searching Unglesbee’s home, investigators also found an empty, unmailed envelope addressed to a congressional office in Washington, D.C.</p><p>The complaint against Unglesbee does not identify the four congressional recipients by name, though Quigley and Schakowsky, whose offices each received a second round of letters, issued separate statements indicating the arrest was in connection with the letters their offices had received.</p>

entries.title: Bears race to 5-2 start, but winning NFC North remains crucial to Super Bowl hopes
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> have been talking Super Bowl ever since the end of last season, and things got a bit louder when <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/31/jeffery-simmons-trade-bears-gm-ryan-poles-pursues-legendary-stuff-as-super-bowl-chase-officially-begins" target="_blank" >they traded for star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons</a> last week.</p><p>Before they get to all that, however, it’s going to be brutal surviving the NFC North.</p><p>As good as the Bears felt about standing 5-2 going into their game Monday at the defending champion Seahawks — and rightfully so — that left them in third place in their own division and just inside the cut for the playoffs.</p><p>The Bears, of course, don’t think they’re the third-best team in the division, and neither do the oddsmakers. Before their game against the Seahawks, the Bears had the sixth-best odds to win the Super Bowl at 12-1, with the Vikings 10th, the Lions 13th and the Packers 15th.</p><p>Sportsbooks don’t decide the standings, but that’s a reasonable outlook on the future of the division rather than going off how it stands at the moment.</p><p>The other relatively safe forecast at this point is that it’s going to be an absolute battle in the last two months of the regular season.</p><p>The NFC North was the only division in the NFL last season to have every team finish with a winning record, and it’s tracking toward repeating that feat. The four teams were a combined 16-3 in non-division games entering Monday.</p><p>There are no freebies in the division, and the Bears already lost what would figure to be their most favorable matchup, falling 9-3 to the Vikings at Soldier Field when quarterback Caleb Williams went down in Week 2. The Vikings are 6-1. And while the consensus is they won’t be able to sustain that level, they have the No. 2 defense in the league and had a lead against the Lions with five minutes left Sunday at Ford Field before taking their first loss.</p><p>The Bears are in a hole at 0-2 in the division — the other loss was a blowout defeat to the Packers at Lambeau Field with Tyson Bagent at quarterback — and will have to make up ground down the stretch. They visit the Lions on Thanksgiving, then close the season hosting the Packers and Lions in Weeks 16 and 17 before visiting the Vikings in Week 18.</p><p>The Bears managed to win the division last season despite going 2-4 in it, but they were the first team to do that since 2010, and the odds of pulling it off again are slim.</p><p>There will be minimal margin for error for the Bears, given what a favorable draw the NFC North got in the scheduling model this season. Every team in the division is playing the NFC South (they’re 7-2 against that group so far) and AFC East (5-1).</p><p>The teams also each will face a squad from the AFC South, where the Jaguars are the only club in the division that isn’t a disaster. The Bears will host them in Week 13, whereas everyone else in the NFC North will play a team that’s 2-5 or worse right now.</p><p>It’s only going to get tougher, too, with the Packers expecting to get star linebacker Micah Parsons back from a knee injury soon and the Lions and Vikings weighing whether to make big moves before the trade deadline next Tuesday.</p><p>Winning the division is crucial to the Bears’ championship hopes because it would change their playoff path completely. After taking the NFC North last season, they had two home playoff games. Had they and the 49ers reached the NFC Championship Game instead of the Rams and Seahawks, that would have been at Soldier Field, too.</p><p>The visit Monday to thunderous Lumen Field emphasized how important playing at home would be. Opponents don’t want to come here any more often than they have to.</p><p>The first question the Bears must answer is whether they’re truly better than the other three teams in their division.</p><p>• They can claim that with the Packers on the grounds of beating them twice in three games last season, including in the playoffs, and put a justifiable asterisk on the loss last month at Lambeau Field because they didn’t have Williams.</p><p>• They can’t make a peep when it comes to the Lions, who destroyed them early last season and clamped down on their offense at the end of it.</p><p>• They can shake off the early loss to the Vikings as an anomaly, but they can’t dismiss how well defensive coordinator extraordinaire Brian Flores outmaneuvered Williams and coach Ben Johnson that day. He’s good enough to do it again.</p><p>The Bears will get a chance to make definitive statements on all three fronts at the end of the season. It’s a near-certainty the division will be tight going into those last three weeks, and the Bears probably will need a sweep of those games to come out on top.</p>

entries.title: Michael Wilbon, longtime ESPN commentator, is taking a leave of absence for 'health issues'
entries.summary: <p>Michael Wilbon is taking a break.</p><p>The longtime ESPN commentator and co-host of the network's popular "Pardon the Interruption" talk show alongside good friend Tony Kornheiser announced Monday he is taking a leave of absence because of what he described as "multiple health issues."</p><p>Wilbon, a Chicago native who turns 68 later this month, wrote in a post on X that he is taking a trip to "the injured list" but added he hopes it is "not an extended one."</p><p>While Wilbon, who is also featured on ESPN's NBA coverage, declined to go into full detail about what he is facing, he said during his weekly appearance on Kornheiser's podcast on Monday that he is diabetic and that is "part of what I'm dealing with now, but not the entirety of it."</p><p>Wilbon's last appearance on "PTI," which recently celebrated its 25th anniversary and is credited with revolutionizing television's "sports debate" format, was on Oct. 26.</p><p>"I didn't do the show for a week because I was just exhausted," Wilbon told Kornheiser. "Beyond exhausted, lifeless. And this has been going on for a while."</p><p>Wilbon, a Northwestern alum and member of the school's board of trustees, stressed that his decision is not a retirement and he plans to return at some point, adding that his symptoms became too significant to ignore.</p><p>"I have to listen," he said to Kornheiser. "I've got things going on that are forcing me to listen."</p><p>The show, in part, is a byproduct of the friendship of Wilbon and Kornheiser, who became colleagues at the Washington Post in the 1980s.</p><p>"I have loved sparring and hosting PTI with Tony every single day these past 25 years," Wilbon wrote. "And I'm incredibly grateful for the support and encouragement of my colleagues as I take this time away to concentrate on me, especially my well-being."<br></p>

entries.title: White Sox skipper Will Venable named a finalist for AL Manager of the Year
entries.summary: <p>In winning 84 games during the regular season, earning the franchise’s first playoff berth in five years and coming one win shy of playing for the American League pennant, the 2026 <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> were a lot better than anyone expected.</p><p>That has a way of leading to hardware for leadership, and on cue, the White Sox’ second-year skipper Will Venable has been named a finalist for AL Manager of the Year. Chad Tracy of the Red Sox, who took over midseason for a club that rallied for wild card berth, and Kevin Cash, the longtime manager of the AL champion Rays, are the other two finalists.</p><p>In his first year on the job, Venable oversaw a 19-win improvement from a 2024 White Sox team that suffered through the losingest season in MLB history. In his second year, Venable seemingly one-upped himself by guiding his club to a 24-win increase and a playoff run that both surprised and electrified the league. Players raved about the unique level of team chemistry that flourished under Venable from the outset of spring training, and continued doing so through postgame media access of their Game 5 loss in the ALDS.</p><p>Addressing reporters after the season, Sox general manager Chris Getz said he expected Venable’s complete coaching staff to return in light of the team’s success, and has expressed interest in ensuring the skipper remains a long-term dugout fixture on the South Side.</p><p>“We've got a really special manager in Will Venable that recognizes the power of the clubhouse,” Getz said last month. “We had so many young players that came up to the big leagues and performed. It wasn't perfect. It didn't need to be perfect and because of that approach, thought process and patience, it kept the group motivated and hungry. Even through their struggles, they were still finding ways to win baseball games.”</p><p>Venable will potentially be the sixth White Sox manager to win the award in franchise history, and the first since Ozzie Guillen in the World Series-winning year of 2005. Jerry Manuel, Jeff Torborg, Tony La Russa and Chuck Tanner are the other past Sox winners.</p>

entries.summary: <p></p><p></p><p> </p><p>Rabbi Capers C. Funnye Jr. was the chief rabbi of Beth Shalom B’nai Zaken Ethiopian Hebrew Congregation on the Southwest Side, one of the largest black synagogues in America.</p><p>He was also former First Lady Michelle Obama's cousin.</p><p>He was credited with serving as a bridge between mainstream, mostly white, Jews and the smaller community of Black Jewish congregations.</p><p>"Not everybody wants to be a bridge, but for Capers, he did want to do this, and was very dedicated to the work," said Robin Washington, who was a co-founder in 1995, along with Rabbi Funnye, of the Alliance of Black Jews.</p><p>"The Alliance only lasted for a few years but we got the word out that Black Jews exist," said Washington, who serves as editor-at-large of the Jewish Forward, an online publication.</p><p>Rabbi Funnye, who began leading the synagogue in Marquette Park in 1985, died Monday from cancer. He was 74.</p><p>"He forced the world to recognize that Black Jews existed whether they wanted to recognize that or not," said longtime congregant and Rabbi Tamar Manasseh. </p><p>"He brought us out of obscurity and said 'Like it or not, we're not going anywhere, enough is enough and I'm tired of Black Jews being on the margins and invisible,' and that was uncomfortable for people, but he didn't care, and he would sit through the discomfort until it got to a point where we would go visit congregations where there were no Blacks, and they would come visit us.</p><p>"He would say 'We have got to learn to actually be tolerant of each other. And he really integrated Judaism in Chicago. He was the first Black Rabbi on the Chicago Board of Rabbis. He broke a lot of barriers and he did it here in Chicago," Manasseh said.</p><p>Rabbi Funnye's congregation posted a note on Facebook Wednesday reading, in part: "Rabbi Funnye has touched countless lives with his spiritual leadership, wisdom, and unwavering commitment to our congregation and the broader Hebrew Israelite community. His legacy of faith, service, and dedication will continue to inspire generations."</p><p>Rabbi Funnye attended Barack Obama's first inauguration in January 2009, and the New York Times ran a profile on him in April of that year.</p><p>"He was very proud of Michelle and Barack, very, very proud," Manasseh said.</p><p>Rabbi Funnye attended eight White House Hanukkah celebrations during the Obama's time there.</p><p>"He never exploited that relationship," said longtime friend Rabbi Baruch Yehudah, who heads up a congregation in Brooklyn. "He respected their space and understood they were not there to pick up his battles. He loved Michelle and liked to talk about funny stories from when she was little."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-8d0000" name="image-8d0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/ddac4e8/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5652x3172+0+298/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fcd%2F83%2F1f82ce00415cab573c9359d1a6b1%2Fxfunnye-cv-vaccine-011521-01.JPG 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/161a7d7/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5652x3172+0+298/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fcd%2F83%2F1f82ce00415cab573c9359d1a6b1%2Fxfunnye-cv-vaccine-011521-01.JPG 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/905f658/2147483647/strip/true/crop/5652x3172+0+298/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fcd%2F83%2F1f82ce00415cab573c9359d1a6b1%2Fxfunnye-cv-vaccine-011521-01.JPG" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Rabbi Capers Funnye receives his first dose of COVID-19 vaccine at Richard J. entries.title: Bears are big dogs after taking bite out of Seahawks, but Jeffery Simmons story still has to play out
entries.summary: <p>If you want to run with the big dogs, you go to Seattle, line up across from the defending Super Bowl champions and take your chances in front of a “Monday Night Football” audience.</p><p>So what if the Seahawks came in with the best all-time winning percentage in prime time of any NFL team? Or if they’d won 28 times in their last 37 night games at Lumen Field?</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> have Caleb Williams. And Ben Johnson. And now — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-grades-seahawks-caleb-williams-jeffery-simmons-luther-burden-jaxon-smith-njigba-chicago-seattle-lumen-nfl" target="_blank" >gosh, is it real?</a> — Jeffery Simmons. There’s no dog big enough to scare them anymore. Nose to nose. Growl for growl. Bite for bite. Let’s get it on.</p><p>At least, that was the Bears’ plan.</p><p>The Seahawks were facing a big dog, too, after all. At least, that was the football universe’s assumption. The moment news broke Thursday that the Bears had traded a pair of first-round picks to the Titans for transcendent defensive tackle Simmons, the Bears became the NFL’s “it” team. A good team? No, a potentially great one. A decent bet to get back to the playoffs? No, a leading Super Bowl contender.</p><p>Pick a gambling site, any gambling site, and what you would have found as Monday’s kickoff arrived was that the Bears had the best odds to win the Super Bowl of any team in the NFC North, the only division in which every team has a winning record. They were right there with the Bills, 49ers, Chiefs, Jaguars and Seahawks. That’s some serious company to keep.</p><p>And as the Bears were closing out a 34-17 win, the odds of them winning it all were getting even shorter.</p><p>Many reporters nearly pulled hamstrings rushing to frame Bears-Seahawks as a “potential preview of the NFC Championship Game,” never mind the fact it's no certainty either of these teams — let alone both of them — will even make the postseason field. The Bears are in good shape at 6-2, but the Seahawks are 4-4 and 2½ games behind the 49ers in the NFC West. </p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-grades-seahawks-caleb-williams-jeffery-simmons-luther-burden-jaxon-smith-njigba-chicago-seattle-lumen-nfl" target="_blank" >Bears’ grades are in. How did they do against the Seahawks?</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-seahawks-score-13-9-halftime-monday-night-football-caleb-williams-ben-johnson-physicality-nfl" >Bears prove they belong among NFC’s elite with decisive 34-17 win vs. defending champs</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>As for the Bears' hopes, this is where I begin to rain on the Super Bowl parade you’ve already been dreaming about with a few cautionary tales.</p><p>Don’t we remember the Cowboys’ early-November trade last year for perennial Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams? That blockbuster deal was intended to be a season saver, which, of course, it wasn’t. The Cowboys have gone 7-9 since then, owner Jerry Jones having last been seen cursing from his suite Sunday as the finishing touches were put on another humiliating defeat.</p><p>Don’t we remember the 7-2 Colts trading two first-rounders for cornerback Sauce Gardner last year? It worked out so well, the Colts are 3-13 since then, fired general manager Chris Ballard and are in fire-sale mode.</p><p>Just before last season, the Packers traded two first-rounders for edge rusher extraordinaire Micah Parsons, then gave him a $186 million contract extension ($112 million of it guaranteed). He tore an ACL in their 14th game, they crumbled down the stretch and now they’re still waiting for him to work his way back onto the field.</p><p>When the Rams went all-in to get sack king Myles Garrett before this season, did they imagine themselves eight games in, at 4-4, and Garrett having zero sacks after missing seven games with a knee injury? Of course they didn’t, yet here they are.</p><p>The Bears have gone all-in, too.</p><p>“I know the ‘all-in’ narrative is there,” GM Ryan Poles said, “[but] we were all-in from the moment we started training camp this year.”</p><p>Simmons’ arrival kicked everything up a notch, though. The Bears are big dogs now. Or are they?</p><p>It’s boom or bust. That’s as clear as a Great Dane’s bark.</p><h3><b>TOMORROW’S HEADLINES</b></h3><p><b>Caleb Williams for MVP? </b>Beating top opponents at night with the world watching is what elite QBs do. About that ceiling? The thing is, there might not be one.</p><p><b>The Jeffery Simmons Factor: </b>Put that bad fella at the tip of the defensive spear and — just like that — everything changes. Does “D” stand for “dominate” going forward?</p><p><b>Look Out, NFC North: </b>Are the Bears — despite their 0-2 start in division games — going to win the North again? You’d better believe they’re the favorites now.</p>

entries.title: 2 officers, 2 civilians hospitalized after CPD vehicle collides with car in Chicago Lawn
entries.summary: <p>Four people, including two police officers, were hospitalized after a Chicago police car collided with another car in Chicago Lawn Monday night, police said.</p><p>The CPD vehicle was driving with its lights and sirens on just before 7 p.m. when it collided with another car in the 6700 block of South California Avenue, according to Chicago police.</p><p>Both the driver and passenger of the other vehicle were taken to Advocate Christ Medical Center, where the man, who was driving, was in good condition and the woman was in fair condition. Two officers suffered minor injuries and were taken to a nearby hospital where they are both listed in good condition.</p><p>Both vehicles suffered significant damage. The front end of the CPD vehicle, a Ford Explorer, had been crushed. The passenger side of the civilian vehicle, a dark-colored Honda Accord, was caved in. Air bags in both vehicles had deployed.</p><p>No other details of the crash, including which driver was at fault, were released.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-600000" name="image-600000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/48cd06a/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F56%2F35%2F8117e63742a29ea173ff256d5d9d%2Fcpdcrash-261103-3.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/1cc4209/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F56%2F35%2F8117e63742a29ea173ff256d5d9d%2Fcpdcrash-261103-3.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/0f60cbf/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+158/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F56%2F35%2F8117e63742a29ea173ff256d5d9d%2Fcpdcrash-261103-3.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="A Honda Accord with a crushed passenger side and deployed airbags after a collision with a Chicago Police Department SUV. entries.title: Blackhawks lose Patrick Kane and early lead in defeat
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> let another opportunity to build on one of their best performances of the season slip away Monday.</p><p>An early two-goal lead quickly was drowned out by five unanswered Avalanche goals in a 5-2 loss Monday, dropping the Hawks to a woeful 4-10-1 this season.</p><p>The news got even worse for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/02/blackhawks-new-green-jerseys-nhl-hometown-remix" target="_blank" >green-clad</a> Hawks when Patrick Kane left during the second period with what coach Jeff Blashill later called an upper-body injury. He’ll miss at least a couple of games.</p><p>Blashill took offense with the implication that the Hawks’ work ethic was as poor Monday as it was last week against the Red Wings. Indeed, it wasn’t that poor.</p><p>But those defeats eliminated the possibility that the games against the Kings and Bruins — which Blashill called two of the Hawks’ five best games in the last four years, based on an internal metric — could turn into major turning points.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Blackhawks postgame thoughts in video form: <a href="https://t.co/mLRfKFR5WM">pic.twitter.com/mLRfKFR5WM</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2117485570695807434?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 3, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>‘‘We’ve talked about this since I’ve been here: It’s an every-night league,’’ forward Oliver Moore<b> </b>said. ‘‘There’s teams throughout the league that do it, that bring that full compete.</p><p>‘‘I think that everyone in here wants it — like, really wants it — but we have to go out there and show that every night. There were moments in tonight’s game where we took control and showed it, but it’s just [about] elongating it over the full 60 [minutes].’’</p><p>Blashill claimed the Hawks’ internal scoring-chance tracking actually gave them a 17-16 edge in that category, but he acknowledged they committed too many penalties.</p><p>The Avalanche finally converted on their fifth power play to take the lead for good late in the second period.</p><p>‘‘They won the game, but . . . if you take the emotion or the score out from clouding your vision, it’s a pretty even game, and we lose it,’’ Blashill said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Avs goal: Nazem Kadri tips in a point shot for his second goal of the game. <a href="https://t.co/r0r8L40Y8d">pic.twitter.com/r0r8L40Y8d</a></p>— BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) <a href="https://x.com/BlackhawksFocus/status/2117447002116284903?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 3, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p>

entries.title: Bears' grades are in. How did they do against the Seahawks?
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-seahawks-score-13-9-halftime-monday-night-football-caleb-williams-ben-johnson-physicality-nfl" target="_blank" >Bears 34, Seahawks 17</a>.</p><p>Eyes opened everywhere.</p><p>Super Bowl thoughts rattling around the heads of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> fans everywhere.</p><p>Is it 1985 all over again?</p><p>Holy cow, that was impressive. Let's get to the grades:</p><h3><b>QUARTERBACK — A</b></h3><p>Seventeen plays. Eighty yards. Eight and a half minutes. Against the top-ranked defense in the NFL — and in one of the toughest environments for a road team in sports — Caleb Williams calmly, coolly directed the first touchdown drive allowed by the Seahawks on an opponent’s opening possession in 27 games. It was a monster drive that said, “We’re here. More importantly, I’m here. Get to know me.” Williams got Colston Loveland going, then Luther Burden, then Rome Odunze. He kept the ball out of harm’s way. On his best play, he stepped his tree-trunk legs out of the grasp of Pro Bowl tackle Leonard Williams’ and hit Odunze for 22 yards on the third-quarter drive that put the Bears up 20-9. “Superstar” is the word now — go ahead and use it freely.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Caleb Williams became the first player with 200+ passing yards against the Seahawks this season on this play<a href="https://t.co/eBATND2yrE">pic.twitter.com/eBATND2yrE</a></p>— Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) <a href="https://x.com/UnderdogNFL/status/2117454587837968768?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 3, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>RECEIVERS — B-PLUS</b></h3><p>Outside of tight end Loveland’s fourth-quarter fumble that set up the Seahawks for a 25-yard touchdown drive and two-point conversion to make it a 20-17 game, it was a great night for the pass catchers. Odunze claimed the deep middle as his territory, even making another of his apparently signature catches by reaching far behind his body — against its momentum — to snare a bullet. Burden, who had a 1-yard touchdown among his seven catches, continues to be open whenever Williams looks for him. Loveland, who also had seven catches, has put his slow start to the season deep in the rearview mirror. You just can’t put the ball on the ground, though.</p><h3><b>RUNNING GAME — B</b></h3><p>What a grind it was to get anything going on the ground against a team that hasn’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in its last 37 games. But the Bears converted a big fourth-and-one on their opening drive, D’Andre Swift getting five yards over the right side of the line (where have we seen that before?). And by the end, even though Swift averaged 2.6 yards per carry, he had 69 yards and three touchdowns and, lordy, you’d take that 17 weeks a season if you could.</p><h3><b>DEFENSIVE LINE — A</b></h3><p>No need to ask on Tuesday why every kid in Bears country seems to be going to school with bright orange sleeves showing. It’s because defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is their new hero. The brand-new Bear had an instant and major impact, recording his first sack with the team, helping linebacker Devin Bush blow up a screen pass, creating steady pressure and yapping nonstop at the Seahawks. Man, what attitude! Montez Sweat was similarly disruptive, exactly what the Bears hoped for in pairing him with his former college teammate. Austin Booker and James Lynch earned props, too, and not just because Booker tipped a pass that Lynch intercepted in nails-in-the-coffin time.</p><h3><b>REST OF THE DEFENSE — A-MINUS</b></h3><p>Linebacker Bush was everywhere, from hammering QB Sam Darnold with a huge hit on a scramble to sacking him later on. The Seahawks just plain couldn’t run the ball. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson took his eyes off Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a beat and got toasted for a 43-yard touchdown as a result. Corner Jaylon Johnson whiffed on another routine-looking tackle attempt, allowing Smith-Njigba to run 21 yards after a catch. On the whole, though, well done by all.</p><h3><b>SPECIAL TEAMS — A-MINUS</b></h3><p>Booker’s field-goal block was one of the biggest plays of the game, keeping the lead at 11. Cairo Santos was pure on every kick, including a pair of field goals. Does anybody in the league go harder in punt coverage than Jahdae Walker? Near disaster came when Tory Taylor’s first punt was deflected; luckily for the Bears, it bounced and rolled and ended up going for 45 yards anyway.</p><h3><b>COACHING — A</b></h3><p>Ben Johnson’s best regular-season win? The Bears looked as good as any team has in any game this season. To pull that off in Seattle required top-notch preparation, no doubt.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-big-plan-coming-together-beautifully-as-34-17-win-over-seahawks-pushes-them-to-best-start-since-2012" target="_blank" >Bears’ big plan coming together beautifully as 34-17 win over Seahawks pushes them to best start since 2012</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-seahawks-score-13-9-halftime-monday-night-football-caleb-williams-ben-johnson-physicality-nfl" >Bears prove they belong among NFC’s elite with decisive 34-17 win vs. defending champs</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Bears' big plan coming together beautifully as 34-17 win over Seahawks pushes them to best start since 2012
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> are watching their plans click into place, and it’s beautiful.</p><p>It’s been a while since they felt like this, watching the right coach, the right quarterback and the right defensive star hit all at the same time in a 34-17 win over the defending champion Seahawks on Monday. After knocking off each of the teams from last season’s Super Bowl in consecutive weeks, the Bears are very much pushing toward their own run to one.</p><p>After years of haphazard moves, ambiguous strategies and mismatched timelines, everything finally seems to be moving in the right direction. At 6-2, they’re off to their best start since 2012.</p><p>The Bears never trailed, though the Seahawks clawed back into the game to cut the lead to 20-17 early in the fourth quarter, and closed the game emphatically with two touchdowns.</p><p>They ended it when defensive end Austin Booker deflected a pass by Sam Darnold for an interception by fellow defensive lineman James Lynch with 5:52 left. That set the Bears up at the Seahawks’ 6-yard line, and they quickly put the game away on D’Andre Swift’s third touchdown run of the night.</p><p>Bears coach Ben Johnson outpunched the ultimate counterpart in Seahawks coach and defensive mastermind Mike Macdonald, and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen was on top of nearly everything Seattle tried offensively.</p><p>Quarterback Caleb Williams was strong throughout, even as the rushing attack stalled, receivers dropped passes and tight end Colston Loveland lost a fumble in the fourth quarter. He completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions for a 101.0 passer rating, becoming the first player this season to top 200 yards passing against Seattle’s overwhelming defense.</p><p>And then there’s defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.</p><p>As if the Bears needed it after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/31/jeffery-simmons-trade-bears-gm-ryan-poles-pursues-legendary-stuff-as-super-bowl-chase-officially-begins" >feeling confident enough to trade two first-round picks to the Titans for him last week</a>, they got instant confirmation that he is a game-changer for their defense.</p><p>Simmons got his first sack as a Bear when he dropped Darnold for a loss in the first quarter. Then, early in the third, the Bears got the snapshot they were looking for when they acquired him.</p><p>On second-and-10 from his own 27-yard line, Darnold dropped back and had nothing. With Simmons and defensive end Montez Sweat coming from Darnold’s right, Seahawks center Jalen Sundell and guard Grey Zabel doubled Simmons and left right tackle Abraham Lucas alone on Sweat.</p><p>Sweat made it look easy as he rushed inside Lucas and took down Darnold for a seven-yard loss.</p><p>That’s what they mean when they call Simmons “a multiplier,” as many did at Halas Hall last week. A player that disruptive makes life easier for everyone around him.</p><p>It has the potential to change the course of the Bears’ season.</p><p>Chasing a championship is the typical next step of any franchise’s progression after a breakthrough like the Bears had last season by going 11-6, taking the NFC North title and reaching the second round of the playoffs. But while they showed promise, they faced two major questions going into this season:</p><p>1. Can Williams round out his game by adding a foundation of steady, efficient play that maximizes Johnson’s offense?</p><p>2. Can their defense climb into the top third or so of the NFL and provide some support so the offense doesn’t have to win shootouts every week?</p><p>The answer has been yes to both, and there’s no sign of either slowing down.</p><p>Williams is playing like he’s not only the future of the Bears, but the future of the league.</p><p>He’s still doing magical scrambles, even as his gait has a clear hitch because of his ongoing hamstring injury, and making stunning passes, but his precision is what’s destroying defenses. Johnson gave him surefire plays and surrounded him with dynamic weapons, and Williams is making full use of them.</p><p>He met Johnson’s 70% completions standard for the third time in five games and is second in the NFL at 70.9% for the season. He is throwing for 253.4 yards per game, which ranks 11th and would be the second-highest for a season in franchise history.</p><p>All the while, he has just one interception in 158 passes.</p><p>The Bears have never had a quarterback like this.</p><p>Establishing that as a concrete truth this season would’ve been enough of a landmark for the team’s overall trajectory, but everything else is lining up perfectly with Williams’ arrival.</p><p>That convergence is a rarity for the Bears, and it has made them into a legitimate contender.</p>

entries.title: No. 3 Illinois beats Fairleigh Dickinson 120-45
entries.summary: <p>CHAMPAIGN — Andrej Stojakovic and Stefan Vaaks each scored 20 points Monday night as No. 3 Illinois opened its season with a 120-45 win over Fairleigh Dickinson.</p><p>The Fighting Illini made a program-record 19 3-pointers, had six players score in double figures and outrebounded Fairleigh Dickinson 65-21.</p><p>The 75-point margin of victory was the largest for Illinois (1-0) at the State Farm Center, which opened in 1963. The Illini fell seven points short of tying the school record for points in a game.</p><p>Quinton Coleman had 13 points and 10 rebounds, Ethan Brown added 12 points and nine rebounds, and Zavier Zens also finished with 12 points for Illinois — each in his collegiate debut.</p><p>Tomislav Ivisic scored 10 in the 7-footer's 30th game with multiple 3s.</p><p>David Jevtic had 13 points for Fairleigh Dickinson (0-1), which shot 28% from the field (17 of 61).</p><p>Illinois played without AP preseason All-American David Mirkovic. The 6-foot-9 sophomore forward underwent an appendectomy Saturday and is out indefinitely. Mirkovic also is recovering from early August foot surgery.</p><p>The Illini's injured list grew Monday when Jake Davis hurt his shoulder midway through the first half and did not return.</p><p>Illinois went on a 24-0 run late in the first half, during which Fairleigh Dickinson called its final timeout, and led 67-20 at halftime. The teams attempted a combined 48 3-pointers in the first half, with the Illini going 12 of 31 and the Knights 1 of 17.</p><p>The Illini improved to 108-14 in season openers. They've won 10 straight since Brad Underwood's first season as coach in 2017.</p><p>Farleigh Dickinson finished 11-21 last season. The Knights have had three straight losing seasons since upsetting No. 1 seed Purdue as a No. 16 seed in the 2023 NCAA Tournament.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Fairleigh Dickinson:</b> Plays at Butler on Wednesday.</p><p><b>Illinois:</b> Will host Penn on Thursday.<br></p>

entries.title: The King vs. The Kid as Bulls and Caleb Wilson face off against LeBron
entries.summary: <p>PHILADELPHIA — If someone would have told Tiago Splitter back in 2014 that in 12 years, he would no longer be competing against LeBron James, he would be coaching against him, his reply would have been a simple one.</p><p>“That you’re crazy,” he said with a laugh of that possibility.</p><p>But there Splitter was in Monday’s 126-107 loss to Philadelphia, no longer battling James in two NBA Finals as a member of the Spurs but trying to game plan against him as the coach of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" >Bulls</a> and James now in Year 24 of his NBA career, playing in the City of Brotherly Love.</p><p>“I think I know that guy from somewhere,” Splitter said of James. “No, I’m a big fan. LeBron is unbelievable. Of course, I faced him in two Finals but he’s unbelievable to see him playing and competing at this level. You know we’re the same age and just looking at him and what he’s doing is unbelievable.”</p><p>Quite the night for Splitter in Philadelphia, as he was trying to figure out how his players could slow down an aging legend in James – who finished with 15 points, nine assists and seven rebounds – while continuing to try and raise a potential superstar of his own in rookie Caleb Wilson.</p><p>The James piece of it proved to be much easier, especially since the future Hall of Famer is now more of a chess master, using his IQ to manipulate the court. His days of being an explosive offensive weapon have simmered at age 41.</p><p>Wilson? He’s just getting started on his NBA journey, and as this week has shown, it’s not exactly a quiet arrival for the 20-year-old. He made that very clear in Boston when he was discussing the team’s lethargic play in the loss and said, “I’m 20 and I’ve never been a loser in my whole life so I’m going to try my best to make sure that doesn’t happen, and I’m not ever going to accept being a loser. This is my job to be a leader on this team and it’s all going to start with me, I know that.</p><p>“It’s partially my fault that we started off the way we did, whether I’m the youngest on the team or not. I take ownership for that and it won’t happen again.”</p><p>He doubled down on that a day later, telling reporters, “Nothing that I do, I feel like, is typical.”</p><p>It’s not, and for good reason as he led the team yet again with 24 points. In most locker rooms the veteran players would put talk like that down, keeping the rookie in a rookie place.</p><p>Why it works for Wilson and the Bulls (1-6), however, is because it’s a younger team, it’s a new regime, and more importantly, his teammates know it comes from a place of being genuine rather than filled with bravado.</p><p>That’s why Splitter isn’t concerned about having to navigate comments from his rookie.</p><p>“I don’t see it that way, by any means,” Splitter said when asked if it could be misconstrued as Wilson trying to take over. “I just think he’s a kid that has a lot of expectations that he’s put on himself and he wants to be a great player. He wants everyone around him to be great as well, but I don’t think there’s anything bad with that.”</p><p>And while it’s not the way Splitter would have spoken as a rookie, his circumstances were much different.</p><p>“I like guys to be humble and know where they are, but of course he’s a guy that is genuine and will speak what he is feeling,” Splitter said. “You just got to be careful.</p><p>“It’s almost impossible to have everybody on the same timeline with the rules that the NBA has now, so you’re always going to have young guys, vet guys, you’re always going to have different timelines. There’s no issue there.”</p>

entries.title: 'Broadview 6' case heats up again as ex-FBI boss sues, top federal prosecutor ordered to testify
entries.summary: <p>Chicago’s former FBI boss accused the city’s top federal prosecutor Monday of chasing political prosecutions at the behest of President Donald Trump and officials in Washington and then trying to cast blame when the “Broadview Six” case collapsed in spectacular fashion.</p><p>But by the end of the day, those explosive claims hardly seemed like the most pressing matter for U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros. Instead, a federal judge had finally <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/11/02/broadview-six-boutros-perry" >ordered Boutros to testify</a> about claims he’s made about the failed prosecution of six Operation Midway Blitz protesters.</p><p>Seemingly at the end of her rope, U.S. District Judge April Perry wrote that Boutros and others “must” testify Nov. 16. Then, in a footnote, she wrote that she meant “must” in its “legal sense.”</p><p>“Which is to say it is mandatory,” Perry wrote.</p><p>Boutros did not comment throughout the extraordinary day that saw Douglas DePodesta, the former special agent in charge of the FBI in Chicago, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/11/02/broadview-six-depodesta-boutros-kat-abughazaleh" >file a nine-count lawsuit</a> against Boutros, FBI Director Kash Patel, Attorney General Todd Blanche, the FBI and the Justice Department.</p><p>Boutros is considered the Chicago area’s top federal law enforcement official. He has denied that politics have played any role in his office’s charging decisions, insisting anyone who says otherwise is “an armchair expert who doesn’t know what they’re talking about.”</p><p>DePodesta’s sister-in-law is a defense attorney who represents a member of the “Broadview Six.” In his lawsuit, DePodesta alleged that Boutros falsely told his superiors in Washington that the pair “conspired to destroy the Broadview Six case.”</p><p>Federal law enforcement officials in Chicago routinely cite the importance of partnerships within the law enforcement community, so it’s stunning to see a former FBI boss sue his onetime colleagues — let alone to make such allegations.</p><p>But DePodesta told the Chicago Sun-Times in an interview that “the American people need to know what is happening within their government.”</p><p>“I was forced to leave my job,” DePodesta said. “I was ordered to leave my job.”</p><p>The lawsuit is being handled by U.S. District Judge Matthew Kennelly. Already, it has led to new revelations about what went on behind the scenes in the “Broadview Six” case. More could follow, if Kennelly decides to let the case move forward.</p><p>Meanwhile, Perry lit into the Justice Department for its handling of the “Broadview Six” fallout. She wrote in a seven-page order Monday that Boutros’ statements about the case are “hard to credit” and “nearly unfathomable.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div
